name: copy-denylist
howToUse: Vendor this file verbatim into each repo's copy-lint test. Matching semantics are defined in CLAIMS-RULES.md section 4. Do not edit the vendored copy; change the source here, bump version, and re-vendor.

surfaces.marketing: Public web pages: landing, pricing, use-case, blog, changelog, OG/meta text, llms.txt.
surfaces.app-ui: Signed-in product UI text (console, dashboard, emails the product sends to its own users).
surfaces.outbound: Campaign JSON, cold email templates, launch posts, ad scripts, video voiceover scripts.
surfaces.docs: Public docs, CLI output, README shown on package registries.
surfaces.api-public: JSON returned by unauthenticated or customer-facing API endpoints (status, plans, launch).
surfaces.legal: Terms, privacy, DPA, subprocessors, security and licence pages.

regexDialect: Portable subset valid in JavaScript (new RegExp), Python re and Rust regex: no lookaround, no backreferences, no named groups, no \p{} classes, no inline flags. Case-insensitivity comes from caseSensitive=false, never from the pattern. Word boundaries are written into each pattern with \b; there is no implicit boundary.

exceptTokens: works with the supabase client libraries
compatible with the supabase client libraries
rules.reason: No competitor names in public copy. Client library package names are allowed because compatibility is a verifiable fact, and the install command must be exact. Owner exception 2026-09-28 (CLAIMS-RULES section 7): factual compatibility phrases that name the client libraries are allowed; the bare name in any other phrase still hits.
rules.fix: Say what the product does ("Postgres with auth, storage, realtime and APIs") or name the client library by its package name only.

miss: Works with your existing supabase-js code
Works with the Supabase client libraries

rules.reason: Competitor names that are also ordinary English words; matched case-sensitively to avoid false hits on "neon" or "convex" as adjectives. Owner exception 2026-09-28 (CLAIMS-RULES section 7): the factual phrases "runs on Neon" and "works with Neon" are allowed; the name in any other phrase still hits.
rules.fix: Remove the name. Describe the capability instead.
